description: Canonical rename mapping from removed / deprecated identifiers to their v1 replacements (or to null when the concept was deleted with no direct successor). cotest scanner and downstream migration tooling consume this as the single source of truth for mechanical renames. Replacement=null means there is no automatic substitution; readers / writers MUST follow the migration guidance in 'notes'.

rejection_levels.hard_reject: After replacement, the old identifier MUST NOT appear in current code or wire bytes.
rejection_levels.migration_only: Mechanical replacement window; both forms tolerated for the bounded migration period.
rejection_levels.compat_only: Old form retained only on explicit interop surfaces.
rejection_levels.docs_only: Old form survives in CHANGELOG / migration docs only.

entries.notes: Deleted: track does not carry independent membership. Migrate access to Realm-level cx.member.state or, when a separate discussion boundary is required, use a linked Realm via Flow.discussion_realm_ref.
Deleted: history visibility lives at the Realm boundary.
Deleted: track-scoped read receipt override is explicitly out of v1 scope.
Deleted: policy attaches to the Realm boundary or to a linked discussion Realm via Flow.discussion_realm_ref, not to a track.
List containers are Spaces. Realm remains the boundary concept; Space carries the container shape.
Mechanical rename on timeline event payloads: 'branch' -> 'track'. Track is display-only and inherits access from the Flow's Realm.
Realm/Space inversion: the pre-inversion container model 'Place' is renamed to 'Space'. The pre-inversion security-boundary model 'Space' is renamed to 'Realm'.
Mechanical rename on Flow payload: 'discussion_space_ref' -> 'discussion_realm_ref'. The security boundary for the discussion side of a Flow is Realm post-inversion.

The current 'cx.space.create' is a DIFFERENT active event with container-shape semantic. Migration tooling MUST inspect wire_id plus payload shape (presence of Realm-level fields like security_class / join_rule / history_visibility / policy_server) to disambiguate.

Mechanical rename of capability-action vocabulary: 'cx.space.notification.audit' -> 'cx.realm.notification.audit'. Required by audit reads of per-Flow watch state under the Realm-scoped notification namespace (see error-code-registry note).

Frontier object property used in cx.audit.ryw_receipt, cx.attestation.range_completeness scope (from_frontier/to_frontier), and POST /events response is renamed 'space_frontier' -> 'realm_frontier'. The boundary covered by this frontier is the Realm (replication/security boundary in v1), not an in-Realm Space container. The new name removes a long-standing source of confusion where implementations could mistakenly validate completeness at Space scope.

Directory search operation id is renamed 'cx.directory.search_spaces' -> 'cx.directory.search_realms'. The Directory has always searched Realms (the replication/security boundary), never in-Realm Space containers; the old name was a leftover from the pre-inversion Space=boundary model and could mislead implementations into thinking they should search nested Spaces. HTTP path /directory/search-realms was already aligned; gRPC binding becomes Directory/SearchRealms and MQ binding becomes directory.search_realms.

Directory resolve operation id is renamed 'cx.directory.resolve_space' -> 'cx.directory.resolve_realm'. Resolution is by realm_id / alias / invite_token / signed_link and returns a Realm preview. HTTP path /directory/resolve-realm was already aligned; gRPC binding becomes Directory/ResolveRealm and MQ binding becomes directory.resolve_realm. Response field 'space_preview' is replaced by 'realm_preview' so the result structure matches the Realm boundary being resolved.
Batch identifier dereference is renamed to resolve; selector / cursor reads stay on cx.events.query.
Account aggregate moved out of the Matrix-derived /sync namespace and changed wire delivery from long-poll JSON response to NDJSON streaming frames.
